blocks.prompt: 7 (i) If \(a, b, c, d\) are in G.P., prove that: \(a - b,\ b - c,\ c - d\) are in G.P.
blocks.explanation:
A proof: we must show three new expressions form a G.P.
Three numbers are in G.P. when the ratio of neighbours is the same.
Plan: write \(b, c, d\) using \(a\) and \(r\), take out common factors, compare ratios.
steps:
Given: \(a, b, c, d\) in G.P.
To prove: \(a - b,\ b - c,\ c - d\) are in G.P.
Method: Let the common ratio be \(r\); then
\[b = ar,\ c = ar^2,\ d = ar^3\]
We assume \(a \neq 0\) and \(r \neq 1\), so that no term is zero.

Write each expression in terms of \(a\) and \(r\)
\[a - b = a - ar\]
\[= a(1 - r)\]
\[b - c = ar - ar^2\]
\[= ar(1 - r)\]
\[c - d = ar^2 - ar^3\]
\[= ar^2(1 - r)\]
Why: Take out the common factor; every expression contains \((1 - r)\).

Find the ratios of neighbours
\[\dfrac{ar(1 - r)}{a(1 - r)} = r\]
\[\dfrac{ar^2(1 - r)}{ar(1 - r)} = r\]
Why: \(a\) and \((1 - r)\) cancel; only powers of \(r\) remain.

Conclude
\[\text{common ratio} = r\]
Why: The ratio of the 2nd to the 1st equals the ratio of the 3rd to the 2nd, so the three expressions are in G.P.

Check with numbers
\[a, b, c, d = 1, 2, 4, 8\]
\[-1, -2, -4 \;(\text{ratio } 2)\]
Why: The ratio found matches \(r\) with \(r = 2\).
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(a - b,\ b - c,\ c - d\) are in G.P. with common ratio \(r\).

blocks.prompt: 7 (ii) If \(a, b, c, d\) are in G.P., prove that: \(a^{2} - b^{2},\ b^{2} - c^{2},\ c^{2} - d^{2}\) are in G.P.
blocks.explanation:
A proof: we must show three new expressions form a G.P.
Three numbers are in G.P. when the ratio of neighbours is the same.
Plan: write \(b, c, d\) using \(a\) and \(r\), take out common factors, compare ratios.
steps:
Given: \(a, b, c, d\) in G.P.
To prove: \(a^2 - b^2,\ b^2 - c^2,\ c^2 - d^2\) are in G.P.
Method: Let the common ratio be \(r\); then
\[b = ar,\ c = ar^2,\ d = ar^3\]
We assume \(a \neq 0\) and \(r \neq \pm 1\), so that no term is zero.

Write each expression in terms of \(a\) and \(r\)
\[a^2 - b^2 = a^2 - a^2r^2\]
\[= a^2(1 - r^2)\]
\[b^2 - c^2 = a^2r^2 - a^2r^4\]
\[= a^2r^2(1 - r^2)\]
\[c^2 - d^2 = a^2r^4 - a^2r^6\]
\[= a^2r^4(1 - r^2)\]
Why: Take out the common factor; every expression contains \((1 - r^2)\).

Find the ratios of neighbours
\[\dfrac{a^2r^2(1 - r^2)}{a^2(1 - r^2)} = r^2\]
\[\dfrac{a^2r^4(1 - r^2)}{a^2r^2(1 - r^2)} = r^2\]
Why: \(a^2\) and \((1 - r^2)\) cancel; only powers of \(r\) remain.

Conclude
\[\text{common ratio} = r^2\]
Why: The ratio of the 2nd to the 1st equals the ratio of the 3rd to the 2nd, so the three expressions are in G.P.

Check with numbers
\[a, b, c, d = 1, 2, 4, 8\]
\[-3, -12, -48 \;(\text{ratio } 4)\]
Why: The ratio found matches \(r^2\) with \(r = 2\).
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(a^2 - b^2,\ b^2 - c^2,\ c^2 - d^2\) are in G.P. with common ratio \(r^2\).

blocks.prompt: 7 (iii) If \(a, b, c, d\) are in G.P., prove that: \(a^{2} + b^{2},\ b^{2} + c^{2},\ c^{2} + d^{2}\) are in G.P.
blocks.explanation:
A proof: we must show three new expressions form a G.P.
Three numbers are in G.P. when the ratio of neighbours is the same.
Plan: write \(b, c, d\) using \(a\) and \(r\), take out common factors, compare ratios.
steps:
Given: \(a, b, c, d\) in G.P.
To prove: \(a^2 + b^2,\ b^2 + c^2,\ c^2 + d^2\) are in G.P.
Method: Let the common ratio be \(r\); then
\[b = ar,\ c = ar^2,\ d = ar^3\]
\(a \neq 0\), and \(1 + r^2\) is never zero for real \(r\), so no term is zero.

Write each expression in terms of \(a\) and \(r\)
\[a^2 + b^2 = a^2 + a^2r^2\]
\[= a^2(1 + r^2)\]
\[b^2 + c^2 = a^2r^2 + a^2r^4\]
\[= a^2r^2(1 + r^2)\]
\[c^2 + d^2 = a^2r^4 + a^2r^6\]
\[= a^2r^4(1 + r^2)\]
Why: Take out the common factor; every expression contains \((1 + r^2)\).

Find the ratios of neighbours
\[\dfrac{a^2r^2(1 + r^2)}{a^2(1 + r^2)} = r^2\]
\[\dfrac{a^2r^4(1 + r^2)}{a^2r^2(1 + r^2)} = r^2\]
Why: \(a^2\) and \((1 + r^2)\) cancel; only powers of \(r\) remain.

Conclude
\[\text{common ratio} = r^2\]
Why: The ratio of the 2nd to the 1st equals the ratio of the 3rd to the 2nd, so the three expressions are in G.P.

Check with numbers
\[a, b, c, d = 1, 2, 4, 8\]
\[5, 20, 80 \;(\text{ratio } 4)\]
Why: The ratio found matches \(r^2\) with \(r = 2\).
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(a^2 + b^2,\ b^2 + c^2,\ c^2 + d^2\) are in G.P. with common ratio \(r^2\).
